subject: Use RAppArmor to knit report in a shiny-app

messages.author: a814dd0eade31e3e
messages.subject: Use RAppArmor to knit report in a shiny-app
parts:
In my app a user can create an rmarkdown report. However, knitting it is a security risk and is disabled on a server. Is it possible to add something like RAppArmor to shinyappsio? https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/RAppArmor/index.html

As an example, see the link below (R > Report). When run locally, clicking the 'Knit report' button generates an HTML report.

https://vnijs.shinyapps.io/analytics/?SSUID=bd88dfc0c4

messages.author: e84e7628b5f8a3e1
messages.subject: Re: [shinyapps-users] Use RAppArmor to knit report in a shiny-app
parts: We've had a couple requests for supporting RAppArmor, but we haven't addressed them yet. But that doesn't mean its not something we could support. Out of curiosity, What type of security problems are you trying to avoid using RAppArmor on shinyapps.io? Applications running on shinyapps.io are already isolated using containers.

messages.author: a814dd0eade31e3e
messages.subject: Re: [shinyapps-users] Use RAppArmor to knit report in a shiny-app
parts: If a user knits a report they can execute arbitrary R-code. By using containers you avoid that a user could crash a server but they could still crash a an app that other users are working with. For example, in my app there is a sessions list in the global environment and I'd want to make sure that a user couldn't (accidentally) delete it.

On Friday, April 1, 2016 at 6:50:32 AM UTC-7, Andy Kipp wrote:
We've had a couple requests for supporting RAppArmor, but we haven't addressed them yet. But that doesn't mean its not something we could support. Out of curiosity, What type of security problems are you trying to avoid using RAppArmor on shinyapps.io? Applications running on shinyapps.io are already isolated using containers.
